example.text: 这本小说写得非常精彩，很（ ）一看。

items.text: 学习外语一定要（ ）下去，不能今天学明天不学。
items.explain: “坚持下去” = keep at it. The second half (不能今天学明天不学) describes not giving up, and only 坚持 takes the complement 下去 here.

items.text: 我很喜欢吃水果，（ ）是西瓜。
items.explain: 尤其 (“especially”) picks out one member of a group just mentioned: fruit in general → 西瓜 in particular. The pattern is “…，尤其是…”.

items.text: 请大家（ ）顺序排队上车。
items.explain: 按照 is a preposition meaning “according to”: 按照顺序 = in order. The blank comes before a noun (顺序) and needs a preposition, which rules out the verbs and adverbs.

items.text: 他平时成绩很一般，没想到这次考试（ ）得了第一名。
items.explain: 竟然 marks a surprising result. 没想到 (“unexpectedly”) and the contrast with 成绩很一般 call for it; it is an adverb, so it goes right before the verb 得了.

items.text: 年轻人刚开始工作的时候，最重要的是（ ）经验。
items.explain: 积累经验 (“build up experience”) is a fixed verb–object pair. The blank needs a verb that takes 经验 as its object.

example.text:
A：今天外面的（ ）是多少？
B：零下五度，出门多穿点儿衣服。

items.text:
A：你去超市的时候，能不能（ ）帮我买瓶牛奶？
B：没问题，还要别的吗？
items.explain: 顺便 = “while you're at it”: the main errand is going to the supermarket, and buying milk is done on the way. It goes before the verb phrase 帮我买.

items.text:
A：明天的会你能参加吗？
B：我明天要去上海出差，（ ）参加不了了。
items.explain: 恐怕 (“I'm afraid…”) softens an unwelcome guess. B is away on business, so B probably can't come: 恐怕参加不了了.

items.text:
A：你们两个说了半天，（ ）谁说得对？
B：我也不清楚，你去问问老师吧。
items.explain: 到底 pushes for a final answer in a question (“who on earth is right?”). 说了半天 shows the speaker is tired of waiting and wants the conclusion.

items.text:
A：别忘了明天早上八点开会。
B：谢谢你（ ）我，我差点儿忘了。
items.explain: 提醒 + person = remind someone. A has just reminded B about the meeting, and B says thanks for it; 差点儿忘了 confirms it.

items.text:
A：小王请你帮忙，你同意帮他了吗？
B：我最近实在太忙了，只好（ ）了他。
items.explain: 拒绝 + person = turn someone down. B is too busy to help, and 只好 (“had no choice but to”) leads into the refusal.

example.text: 这里的冬天很冷，最低（ ）有零下二十度。

items.text: 我家（ ）公司不远，走路十分钟就到。
items.explain: “距离” (“distance”) is a verb here: “我家距离公司不远” = my home is not far from the company. The pattern is 距离 + place + 远/近. “温度” is temperature, so it cannot link two places.

items.text: 我已经说了很多次了，可是孩子（ ）不听。
items.explain: “仍然” (“still, yet”) shows nothing has changed despite repeated effort: said many times, “可是孩子仍然不听”. It is an adverb before the verb 不听; “随便” does not fit the meaning.

items.text: 明天的会很重要，你（ ）我一下，别让我忘了。
items.explain: “提醒” (“to remind”) takes a person: “提醒我一下”, and the follow-up “别让我忘了” confirms the meaning. “提醒” is a verb; “随便” and “仍然” make no sense after “你”.

items.text: 他感冒了，咳嗽得很（ ）。
items.explain: “咳嗽得很厉害” uses “得” + degree complement: “厉害” (“severe, serious”) describes how bad the cough is. “厉害” is an adjective; the other bank words are nouns or adverbs and do not fit here.

items.text: 你想吃什么就点什么，别客气，（ ）点。
items.explain: “随便” (“as you like, casually”) fits “想吃什么就点什么，别客气，随便点”: order freely. It is used as an adverb before the verb 点. “仍然” means still and does not fit.

example.text: 这本书的内容很（ ），大家都很喜欢。

items.text: 他刚来北京，还不太（ ）这里的天气。
items.explain: “适应” (“to adapt to”) takes an object: “适应这里的天气”. The context, just arrived in Beijing, points to getting used to the climate. “丰富” and “共同” do not take 天气 as object.

items.text: 从这儿到机场（ ）要一个小时。
items.explain: “至少” (“at least”) gives a minimum amount: “至少要一个小时” = takes an hour at the very least. It is an adverb before 要 plus a time amount. “专门” does not express quantity.

items.text: 这次他考得很好，老师（ ）了他。
items.explain: “表扬” (“to praise”) matches “考得很好” (did well on the exam): the teacher praises him. It is a verb followed by 了 and the person. The other verb-like word, “适应”, does not fit.

items.text: 这家店是（ ）卖儿童衣服的。
items.explain: “专门” (“specially, exclusively”) appears in “是专门……的”: this shop specializes in selling children’s clothes. It is an adverb before the verb 卖. “共同” needs a joint action.

items.text: 我们俩有很多（ ）的爱好。
items.explain: “共同” (“common, shared”) modifies 爱好 with 的: “共同的爱好” = shared hobbies, fitting “我们俩”. “丰富” (rich) usually describes content or experience, not hobbies shared by two people.

example.text: 按照公司的（ ），上班不能迟到。

items.text: 你去邮局的时候，（ ）帮我寄一封信吧。
items.explain: “顺便” (“by the way, while you are at it”) fits “去邮局的时候……帮我寄一封信”: the favour is done on the same trip. It is an adverb before the verb 帮.

items.text: 他学习很好，但是一点儿也不（ ）。
items.explain: “骄傲” (“proud, conceited”) after “一点儿也不”: he studies well but is not arrogant. The “但是” contrast supports it. It is an adjective that takes the 不 negation here.

items.text: 医生让我每天（ ）吃药。
items.explain: “按时” (“on time, at the set time”) goes before the verb 吃药: the doctor says to take medicine at fixed times each day. “规定” is a noun or verb and does not fit.

items.text: 天这么黑，我（ ）要下雨了。
items.explain: “估计” (“to estimate, reckon”) expresses a guess from evidence: the sky is dark, so “我估计要下雨了”. It is a verb followed by a clause. “规定” (to stipulate) does not express a guess.

items.text: 他不但会说汉语，（ ）还会说一点儿上海话。
items.explain: “不但……，甚至……” is an escalation: not only Chinese, “甚至” (“even”) a bit of Shanghainese. 甚至 introduces the more surprising point; “顺便” does not link two clauses this way.

example.text: 教孩子一定要有（ ）。

items.text: 她在这次比赛中（ ）了第一名。
items.explain: “获得” (“to obtain, win”) collocates with “第一名”: won first place in the contest. It is a verb followed by 了. “缺少” (lack) has the opposite sense.

items.text: 你快点儿走吧，（ ）就来不及了。
items.explain: “否则” (“otherwise”) introduces the bad result of not hurrying: “快点儿走，否则就来不及了”. It links two clauses as a conjunction. The others are nouns or verbs.

items.text: 他把照片（ ）在了墙上。
items.explain: “挂” (“to hang”) fits a photo on a wall: the 把 sentence “把照片挂在了墙上” needs a verb plus 在 for the location. “棵” is a measure word, not a verb.

items.text: 我家门口有一（ ）大树。
items.explain: “棵” is the measure word for trees: “一棵大树”. The pattern is number + measure word + noun; “挂” is a verb and “耐心” is a noun, so neither can follow 一.

items.text: 这个城市（ ）水，大家要节约用水。
items.explain: “缺少” (“to lack, be short of”) takes 水 as its object: the city lacks water, hence “节约用水”. “获得” (obtain) would contradict the call to save water.

example.text: 这里不（ ）抽烟。

items.text: 晚上一个人去那儿太（ ）了。
items.explain: “太危险了” (“dangerous”): going alone at night is risky. “危险” is an adjective after 太 and before 了. “适合” and “保护” are verbs that need an object.

items.text: 这件衣服很（ ）你，你穿上真好看。
items.explain: “适合” (“to suit”) takes a person as object: the clothes suit you, and “穿上真好看” confirms it. It is a verb after “很”. “保护” and “允许” do not fit clothes.

items.text: 我刚想给你打电话，你（ ）来了。
items.explain: “正好” (“just at that moment, just right”) marks a lucky coincidence: just as I was about to call, you came. It is an adverb before 来. “往往” describes habit, not one event.

items.text: 我们应该（ ）环境，少用塑料袋。
items.explain: “保护环境” (“to protect the environment”) is a fixed collocation, matching “少用塑料袋”. It is a verb with 环境 as object. “允许” (allow) would not suit this meaning.

items.text: 越是简单的问题，（ ）越容易出错。
items.explain: “往往” (“often, tends to”) states a general tendency: the simpler the problem, the more often errors happen. “越是……往往越……” is the pattern. “正好” refers to a single moment, not a tendency.

example.text: 昨天晚上没睡好，我现在特别（ ）。

items.text: 这个时间不太（ ），你再查一下。
items.explain: “准确” (“accurate”) describes the time: not accurate, so “你再查一下” (check again). It is an adjective after “不太”. “辛苦” and “困” describe people, not a time.

items.text: 这几年，城市里汽车的（ ）越来越多。
items.explain: “数量” (“quantity, number”) is a noun, the subject of “越来越多”: the number of cars keeps growing. “准确” and “辛苦” cannot be what is “多”.

items.text: 周末我要（ ）妈妈去医院。
items.explain: “陪” (“to accompany”) takes a person: “陪妈妈去医院” is accompanying Mom to the hospital. It is a verb in the pattern 陪 + person + 去 + place. “困” is an adjective.

items.text: 我买了一本书，（ ）还买了两支笔。
items.explain: “另外” (“in addition, besides”) adds a second item: bought a book, and also two pens. It goes before 还 as a connecting adverb. “数量” is a noun and cannot link clauses.

items.text: 他最近工作特别（ ），每天都加班。
items.explain: “辛苦” (“hard, toilsome”) describes his work: “每天都加班” (overtime daily) explains it. It is an adjective after “特别”. “困” (sleepy) would describe his state, not the work.

example.text: 我们以后经常（ ）吧，这是我的电话号码。

items.text: 这个公园的（ ）很新鲜。
items.explain: “空气” (“air”) is the noun that is “很新鲜” (fresh) in a park. Fresh air is a natural collocation. “负责” and “联系” are verbs and cannot be the subject here.

items.text: 我（ ）想去看电影，后来有事没去成。
items.explain: “本来” (“originally, had intended”) sets up a plan that changed: “后来有事没去成”. It is an adverb before 想. “超过” (exceed) has no plan meaning.

items.text: 这件事由小王（ ），有问题你去问他。
items.explain: “由小王负责” (“be in charge of”) is a pattern: 由 + person + 负责. The next clause “有问题你去问他” says he is the person responsible. “联系” (contact) does not mean being in charge.

items.text: 不好意思，（ ）一下，请问去火车站怎么走？
items.explain: “打扰一下” (“excuse me, sorry to bother you”) is the polite phrase for opening a request to a stranger, after “不好意思”. It is a verb with 一下. “联系一下” would mean contact.

items.text: 今天的温度（ ）了三十五度。
items.explain: “超过” (“to exceed”) takes the figure “三十五度”: the temperature went over 35 degrees. It is a verb followed by 了 and a number. “温度” itself is the subject, not the verb.

example.text: 请大家按（ ）排队上车。

items.text: 昨天的比赛非常（ ），大家都看得很开心。
items.explain: “精彩” (“wonderful, brilliant”) describes a match: “大家都看得很开心” gives the result. It is an adjective after “非常”. “严格” and “普遍” do not describe a game.

items.text: 现在找工作的人很多，（ ）很大。
items.explain: “竞争” (“competition”) fits “找工作的人很多” (many job seekers) and “很大” (intense). “竞争很大” is a common collocation; it is a noun here. “增加” is a verb.

items.text: 我们学校对学生要求很（ ）。
items.explain: “严格” (“strict”) fits “要求很严格”: the school sets strict demands. It is an adjective after “很”, a typical collocation with 要求. “普遍” does not describe demands.

items.text: 这几年，来这个城市工作的人（ ）了很多。
items.explain: “增加了很多” (“to increase”) works with “人”: the number of workers rose. “增加” is a verb followed by 了 and a quantity. “竞争” is a noun, so it cannot follow 人 here.

items.text: 现在用手机付款的情况已经非常（ ）了。
items.explain: “普遍” (“widespread, common”) says paying by phone is now common. It is an adjective after “非常” and before 了. “严格” and “精彩” do not describe how widespread a practice is.

example.text: 外面很冷，你穿件（ ）一点儿的衣服吧。

items.text: 我平时不喝咖啡，只是（ ）喝一次。
items.explain: “偶尔” (“occasionally”) contrasts with “平时不喝” (normally not) and “只是……喝一次” (only once in a while). It is an adverb before the verb 喝. “继续” does not fit.

items.text: （ ）下大雨，今天的比赛推迟了。
items.explain: “由于” (“because of”) opens the cause: heavy rain, so the match was postponed. It starts the sentence as a conjunction with the result in the second clause. “目的” is a noun.

items.text: 我今天（ ）有点儿不舒服，想早点儿回家。
items.explain: “感觉” (“to feel”) takes the description “有点儿不舒服”: I feel a bit unwell, so I want to go home. It is a verb before the clause. “感觉” here carries the speaker’s own feeling.

items.text: 休息十分钟，我们再（ ）开会。
items.explain: “继续” (“to continue”) fits “休息十分钟，再继续开会”: after a break, resume the meeting. It is a verb before another verb 开会. “厚” is only an adjective for thickness.

items.text: 我来中国的（ ）是学习汉语。
items.explain: “我来中国的目的是学习汉语”: “目的” (“purpose, aim”) is a noun and the subject of 是. The structure is 的 + 目的 + 是. “感觉” and “继续” are verbs and do not fit after 的.

example.text:
A：你学的是什么（ ）？
B：我学的是法律。

items.text:
A：从这儿到你家（ ）要多长时间？
B：开车二十分钟左右。
items.explain: “大概” (“approximately”) asks for a rough time; the reply “二十分钟左右” (about twenty minutes) matches it. It is an adverb before 要. “故意” and “条件” do not fit the question.

items.text:
A：你怎么把我的杯子打破了？
B：对不起，我不是（ ）的。
items.explain: “故意” (“on purpose”) fits “我不是故意的”: I did not break the cup deliberately. The pattern “不是……的” follows. “丢” and “抱歉” do not fit this apology.

items.text:
A：我的钱包（ ）了，你看见了吗？
B：没有，你再找找。
items.explain: “丢” (“to lose”) fits a wallet: “我的钱包丢了”, and the reply “你再找找” (look again) confirms it. It is a verb followed by 了. “抱歉” is a feeling, not a loss.

items.text:
A：（ ），让你等了这么久。
B：没关系，我也刚到。
items.explain: “抱歉” (“sorry”) is the apology for making someone wait: “让你等了这么久”. The reply “没关系” confirms it. “故意” would be a poor start, since it is not an apology.

items.text:
A：这个房子的（ ）怎么样？
B：挺好的，有厨房，有卫生间，离地铁也近。
items.explain: “条件” (“conditions, facilities”) is what the reply describes: kitchen, bathroom, and near the subway. “房子的条件” is a normal collocation. “专业” (major, professional) does not describe a flat.

example.text:
A：这个博物馆要买票吗？
B：不用，是（ ）的。

items.text:
A：这儿的（ ）真美！
B：是啊，我们在这儿照张相吧。
items.explain: “景色” (“scenery”) fits “真美” and the plan to take photos there. “这儿的景色” is a typical collocation. “力气” and “免费” do not pair with “美”.

items.text:
A：（ ）你不知道明天放假？
B：真的吗？没人告诉我啊。
items.explain: “难道……?” (“could it be that…?”) is a rhetorical question: don’t you know there is a holiday tomorrow? The reply shows surprise. 难道 starts the sentence and expects a question.

items.text:
A：你还记得我们第一次见面的时候吗？
B：当然记得，（ ）你穿着一件红衣服。
items.explain: “当时” (“at that time”) refers back to the first meeting: back then you were wearing a red coat. It is a time word at the head of the clause. “难道” does not give a time.

items.text:
A：你帮我把这个箱子搬上去吧。
B：太重了，我没那么大（ ）。
items.explain: “没那么大力气” means not strong enough to lift it. “力气” (“physical strength”) is the noun after “大”. “太重了” supports it; “免费” and “景色” make no sense here.

items.text:
A：他说他明天就还你钱。
B：你别信，他已经（ ）我好几次了。
items.explain: “骗” (“to deceive”) fits “你别信”: he has already lied to me several times. It is a verb with the object 我, followed by 好几次. “他说明天还钱” is the lie.

example.text:
A：你尝尝这个菜，（ ）怎么样？
B：挺好吃的。

items.text:
A：明天的会几点开始？
B：还没（ ），我也不知道。
items.explain: “通知” (“to notify”) works with “还没通知，我也不知道”: no one has told us the time yet. It is a verb after “还没”. “肯定” and “讨厌” do not fit this meaning.

items.text:
A：吃完饭我们去公园（ ）吧。
B：好啊，今天天气不错。
items.explain: “散步” (“to take a walk”) fits “吃完饭……去公园散步吧”: a walk after dinner in the park. It is a verb-object word after 去公园. “通知” and “麻烦” do not fit here.

items.text:
A：（ ）你帮我拿一下那本书，好吗？
B：没问题。
items.explain: “麻烦你……” (“sorry to trouble you, could you…”) is a polite request opener. The reply “没问题” accepts. “麻烦” is a verb with a person as object. “讨厌” would be rude.

items.text:
A：你为什么不喜欢他？
B：他总是说假话，我最（ ）说假话的人了。
items.explain: “讨厌” (“to dislike, hate”) fits the reason: he tells lies, so I hate liars. “我最讨厌……的人” is a common pattern. “肯定” and “麻烦” do not express feeling toward people.

items.text:
A：你觉得他会来吗？
B：他（ ）会来，我们昨天已经说好了。
items.explain: “肯定” (“definitely”) expresses certainty, backed by “昨天已经说好了”. It is an adverb before 会来. “通知” and “麻烦” cannot express certainty.

example.text:
A：你的（ ）办好了吗？
B：还没有，下周才能拿到。

items.text:
A：你丈夫对你真好！
B：你是不是很（ ）我？
items.explain: “羡慕” (“to envy”) fits the remark that her husband treats her so well. “是不是很羡慕我” asks if you are envious. It is a verb with the object 我. “熟悉” would not match.

items.text:
A：会议改时间了吗？
B：是的，（ ）到下周三了。
items.explain: “推迟” (“to postpone”) fits a meeting whose time changed: “推迟到下周三” = moved back to next Wednesday. The pattern is 推迟 + 到 + new time. “节约” does not fit.

items.text:
A：你对这儿（ ）吗？
B：当然，我在这儿住了二十年了。
items.explain: “对这儿熟悉吗？” asks whether you are familiar with the place. “熟悉” (“familiar”) is an adjective after 对. The reply “住了二十年” confirms it. 对……熟悉 is the pattern.

items.text:
A：你家的（ ）真大！
B：是啊，朋友来了都在这儿聊天。
items.explain: “客厅” (“living room”) is the place where “朋友来了都在这儿聊天”. The noun after “你家的” and before “真大”. “签证” (visa) and “节约” cannot be “大”.

items.text:
A：你为什么每次出门都把灯关了？
B：为了（ ）用电啊。
items.explain: “节约用电” (“save electricity”) is a fixed collocation, matching the habit of turning off lights. “为了” + verb phrase gives the purpose. “推迟” and “熟悉” do not take 用电.

example.text:
A：请问，（ ）在哪儿？
B：一直往前走，在右边。

items.text:
A：这是什么意思？你能给我（ ）一下吗？
B：好，你听我说。
items.explain: “解释” (“to explain”) fits “这是什么意思？” (what does this mean?) and “你听我说”. “给我解释一下” = explain it to me. It is a verb with 一下. “表格” is a noun.

items.text:
A：请先填一下这张（ ）。
B：好的，用什么笔写？
items.explain: “填表格” (“fill in a form”) is the usual collocation: the verb 填 takes the noun “表格”, and “用什么笔写” fits. “这张” needs a noun. “厕所” and “酸” do not fit.

items.text:
A：这个苹果怎么样？
B：有点儿（ ），不太甜。
items.explain: “酸” (“sour”) describes the apple’s taste, and “不太甜” (not very sweet) agrees. It is an adjective after “有点儿”. “害羞” and “自信” describe people, not fruit.

items.text:
A：你女儿怎么不跟客人说话？
B：她比较（ ），过一会儿就好了。
items.explain: “害羞” (“shy”) explains why the daughter will not talk to guests; she will be fine soon. It is an adjective after “比较”. “自信” (confident) would be the opposite.

items.text:
A：我怕我考不好。
B：你准备得这么好，要有（ ）！
items.explain: “要有自信” (“have confidence”): the encouragement “准备得这么好” answers the fear of failing. “自信” is a noun here, after 有. “害羞” would not comfort anyone.

example.text:
A：你刚才去哪儿了？
B：我去了一（ ）超市。

items.text:
A：你帮我复印一（ ）材料吧。
B：好的，马上去。
items.explain: “份” is the measure word for documents: “一份材料” (one copy of the material). The pattern is 一 + 份 + noun. “趟” counts trips, and “叶子” is a noun, not a measure word.

items.text:
A：这儿可以（ ）吗？
B：对不起，这里不行。
items.explain: “抽烟” (“to smoke”) fits “这儿可以……吗？” asking permission; the refusal “这里不行” follows. It is a verb-object phrase after 可以. “乱” and “可怜” do not fit.

items.text:
A：你看那只小狗，好像找不到家了。
B：真（ ），我们给它点儿吃的吧。
items.explain: “可怜” (“pitiful, poor”) fits a lost puppy that cannot find home; “我们给它点儿吃的” shows sympathy. It is an adjective after “真”. “乱” (messy) does not fit.

items.text:
A：你的房间怎么这么（ ）？
B：我这几天太忙了，没时间收拾。
items.explain: “乱” (“messy”) describes the room, and the reply “没时间收拾” (no time to tidy) explains it. It is an adjective after “这么”. “可怜” would describe a creature, not a room.

items.text:
A：秋天到了。
B：是啊，树上的（ ）都黄了。
items.explain: “叶子” (“leaves”) are what turn yellow on the trees in autumn. It is the noun subject of “都黄了”. “份” and “趟” are measure words and cannot be turned yellow.

example.text:
A：这篇文章是谁（ ）的？
B：是小王，他英语很好。

items.text:
A：我们几点出发？
B：八点，请大家（ ）到。
items.explain: “准时” (“punctual, on time”) fits “八点，请大家准时到”: arrive at eight sharp. It is an adverb before 到. “正式” (formal) does not describe arrival time.

items.text:
A：车快没油了。
B：前面有个（ ），我们去加点儿油吧。
items.explain: “加油站” (“gas station”) is where you get “加点儿油” when the car is nearly out of fuel. It follows 前面有个. “翻译” and “失望” cannot be a place.

items.text:
A：你明天能来吗？
B：（ ）不行，我明天要出差。
items.explain: “恐怕” (“I’m afraid”) softens a refusal: “恐怕不行，我明天要出差”. It is an adverb before 不行 and states a probable negative. “准时” does not express polite refusal.

items.text:
A：参加会议要穿得（ ）一点儿。
B：好，我穿那件黑色的衣服。
items.explain: “正式” (“formal”) fits a meeting: dress more formally, and the reply picks black clothes. “穿得正式一点儿” uses 得 + complement. “失望” and “翻译” do not describe clothing.

items.text:
A：他这次又没考好。
B：是啊，他父母很（ ）。
items.explain: “失望” (“disappointed”) fits parents whose child failed an exam again. It is an adjective after “很”. “他父母很失望” is the natural result. “恐怕” and “准时” do not fit.

example.text:
A：你的汉语说得真（ ）！
B：谢谢，我学了三年了。

items.text:
A：你（ ）想要哪一个？
B：让我再想想。
items.explain: “究竟” (“exactly, on earth”) in a question presses for the real answer: “你究竟想要哪一个”. The reply “让我再想想” shows indecision. It is an adverb before the verb 想要.

items.text:
A：你怎么只吃这么一点儿？
B：我在（ ），晚饭少吃点儿。
items.explain: “减肥” (“to lose weight”) explains why she eats little at dinner. “我在减肥” is a verb-object phrase. “怀疑” and “棒” do not give a reason for eating less.

items.text:
A：这个（ ）里面是什么？
B：是我给你买的礼物。
items.explain: “盒子” (“box”) is the noun after 这个 and before 里面: “这个盒子里面是什么”. The reply mentions a gift, which can be inside a box. “怀疑” and “棒” are not nouns for objects.

items.text:
A：你觉得他说的是真的吗？
B：我有点儿（ ），他说得太好了。
items.explain: “怀疑” (“to doubt”) fits “他说得太好了” (too good to be true). “我有点儿怀疑” expresses mild doubt after the question of whether it is true. “棒” does not express doubt.

items.text:
A：我这次考了一百分！
B：太（ ）了！
items.explain: “太棒了” (“great!”) is the praise for scoring 100. “棒” is an adjective after 太 and before 了. The other bank words are not exclamations of praise.

example.text:
A：周末你想去哪儿？
B：我想去商场（ ）一下，买几件衣服。

items.text:
A：你怎么又写错了？
B：对不起，我太（ ）了。
items.explain: “粗心” (“careless”) explains the repeated mistake: “太粗心了”. It is an adjective after 太. “仔细” (careful) is the opposite. “批评” and “表演” do not describe a person’s habit.

items.text:
A：昨天的节目谁（ ）得最好？
B：我觉得是小李。
items.explain: “表演” (“to perform”) fits “节目” (the programme): who performed best. “表演得最好” uses 得 + complement of degree. “批评” does not take 节目 here.

items.text:
A：先生，请给我看一下您的（ ）。
B：好的，给你。
items.explain: “登机牌” (“boarding pass”) is what is checked when you are asked to show it: “请给我看一下您的登机牌”. It is a noun after 您的. The other words are verbs or adjectives.

items.text:
A：老师为什么（ ）他？
B：因为他上课玩儿手机。
items.explain: “批评” (“to criticize”) fits the reason: he played with his phone in class, so the teacher scolded him. It is a verb with 他 as object. “表演” (perform) does not fit.

items.text:
A：这份材料我看完了，没问题。
B：你再（ ）看一遍，别有错误。
items.explain: “仔细” (“careful, carefully”) is an adverb before 看: look it over once more carefully so there are no errors. “粗心” would be the opposite. “再仔细看一遍” fits the meaning.

example.text: 他说话很（ ），大家都喜欢跟他聊天。

items.text: 不管遇到什么困难，都不要轻易（ ）。
items.explain: “放弃” (“to give up”) fits “不管遇到什么困难，都不要轻易放弃”: don’t give up easily. It is a verb after 轻易. “原谅” and “污染” do not match this encouragement.

items.text: 明天的会很重要，请大家（ ）十分钟到。
items.explain: “提前” (“in advance, ahead of time”) takes a time amount: “提前十分钟到” = arrive ten minutes early, important for a meeting. It is a verb before 十分钟. “原谅” does not.

items.text: 很多垃圾（ ）了这条河。
items.explain: “污染” (“to pollute”) fits rubbish and a river: “很多垃圾污染了这条河”. It is a verb with the object 这条河 and the 了 ending. “详细” and “幽默” cannot take an object.

items.text: 对不起，我不是故意的，请你（ ）我。
items.explain: “原谅” (“to forgive”) follows the apology: “我不是故意的，请你原谅我”. It is a verb with a person as object. “放弃” and “提前” do not respond to an apology.

items.text: 这本书把做菜的方法写得非常（ ），一看就会。
items.explain: “详细” (“detailed”) describes how the recipe is written; “一看就会” shows it is clear. “写得非常详细” uses 得 + complement. “幽默” (humorous) would not explain “一看就会”.

example.text: 这家公司正在（ ）新员工。

items.text: 我们应该（ ）别人的想法。
items.explain: “尊重” (“to respect”) takes 别人的想法 as object: we should respect others’ ideas. It is a verb after “应该”. “勇敢” and “暂时” do not take an object like this.

items.text: 这种药的（ ）很好，吃了两天病就好了。
items.explain: “效果” (“effect, result”) is the noun for how well medicine works: “药的效果很好”, with the proof “两天病就好了”. “吸引” and “暂时” cannot follow 药的.

items.text: 他很（ ），一个人跳进河里把那个孩子带了回来。
items.explain: “勇敢” (“brave”) describes the person who jumped into the river to bring back a child. It is an adjective after “很”. The action in the second half illustrates the trait.

items.text: 这部电影的广告（ ）了很多观众。
items.explain: “吸引” (“to attract”) takes 观众 as object: the ad attracted many viewers. It is a verb followed by 了 and “很多观众”. “招聘” means recruit, and does not suit an audience.

items.text: 经理（ ）不在，你有事可以先跟我说。
items.explain: “暂时” (“temporarily, for now”) says the manager is out only for the moment: “暂时不在，你有事可以先跟我说”. It is an adverb before 不在. “招聘” has no such sense.

example.text: 他是一位很（ ）的作家，写了很多小说。

items.text: （ ）是成功之母。
items.explain: “失败是成功之母” (“failure is the mother of success”) is a proverb. “失败” (“failure”) is the noun subject, set against 成功. The other bank words do not fit the saying.

items.text: 他上课很（ ），总是第一个回答问题。
items.explain: “积极” (“active, positive”) describes his class participation: always first to answer. It is an adjective after “很”. “著名” (famous) and “失败” do not describe attitude.

items.text: 坐地铁比打车能（ ）不少钱。
items.explain: “省钱” (“to save money”): “省” (“to save”) takes 钱 as object, matching the comparison of subway versus taxi. “能省不少钱” fits. “养成” and “区别” take other objects.

items.text: 这两个词的意思有什么（ ）？
items.explain: “区别” (“difference”) is the noun in “有什么区别”, asking how two words differ. The pattern is “A和B有什么区别”. “养成” and “著名” cannot follow 有什么.

items.text: 要从小（ ）早睡早起的好习惯。
items.explain: “养成……习惯” (“to form a habit”) is a fixed collocation: form the good habit of early to bed, early to rise. “养成” is a verb. “省” (save) and “区别” do not take 习惯.

example.text: 谢谢你的（ ），我一定去参加你的生日聚会。

items.text: （ ）刮风下雨，他每天都去跑步。
items.explain: “无论……，都……” means no matter what: “无论刮风下雨，他每天都去跑步”. “无论” starts the clause and is answered by 都. “顺利” and “直接” do not set up a condition.

items.text: 考试前我的（ ）特别大，常常睡不着。
items.explain: “压力” (“pressure”) is the noun that can be “特别大” (very great) before exams and cause sleeplessness. “压力很大” is a common collocation. “邀请” and “重视” are verbs.

items.text: 祝你一路（ ）！
items.explain: “祝你一路顺利” (“have a smooth trip”) is a fixed farewell wish. “顺利” (“smooth, successful”) is an adjective after 一路. “直接” and “压力” do not belong to this phrase.

items.text: 你不用换车，这趟车可以（ ）到机场。
items.explain: “直接” (“directly”) is an adverb before 到: the bus goes straight to the airport, so no transfer. “直接到机场” fits “不用换车”. “顺利” does not mean without transfer.

items.text: 学校非常（ ）学生的安全。
items.explain: “重视” (“to attach importance to”) takes “学生的安全” as object: the school values students’ safety. It is a verb after “非常”. “邀请” (invite) does not suit the object.

example.text: 他给我留下了很深的（ ）。

items.text: 同学之间应该（ ）帮助。
items.explain: “互相帮助” (“help each other”) is a fixed collocation. “互相” is an adverb before the verb, meaning each other. “也许” and “研究” do not fit between classmates.

items.text: 他打了三次电话都没人接，（ ）他已经睡了。
items.explain: “也许” (“perhaps”) gives a guess from evidence: three calls and no answer, so maybe he is asleep. It is an adverb before 他已经睡了. “互相” does not express possibility.

items.text: 科学家们正在（ ）这种病。
items.explain: “研究” (“to research”) takes “这种病” as object: scientists study this disease. “正在研究” = currently researching. “降低” and “符合” do not suit the object.

items.text: 你的条件完全（ ）我们的要求。
items.explain: “符合要求” (“to meet the requirements”) is a standard collocation; “完全符合” says it fits fully. It is a verb with “我们的要求” as object. “印象” is a noun.

items.text: 这个月商店（ ）了价格，买的人更多了。
items.explain: “降低价格” (“to lower the price”) is the collocation, and the result is “买的人更多了”. It is a verb followed by 了. “印象” is a noun, and “符合” would not suit prices.

example.text:
A：你女儿性格怎么样？
B：她很（ ），总是笑。

items.text:
A：电影七点开始，现在六点半，还（ ）吗？
B：打车去的话没问题。
items.explain: “来得及” (“there is still time”) answers whether they can make a film starting at seven when it is half past six. The question form “还来得及吗” is fixed; the reply discusses taking a taxi.

items.text:
A：你怎么不高兴？
B：我刚才（ ）他了，他不是那个意思。
items.explain: “误会” (“to misunderstand”) fits “他不是那个意思”: I misread him. It is a verb followed by 他了. This explains why the other person is unhappy. “商量” does not fit.

items.text:
A：这件事你自己决定吧。
B：不行，我得跟家里人（ ）一下。
items.explain: “商量” (“to discuss, consult”) fits “得跟家里人商量一下”: consult family before deciding. The pattern is 跟 + person + 商量. “误会” does not take 一下 like this.

items.text:
A：你想吃点儿什么甜的？
B：给我来一块（ ）吧。
items.explain: “巧克力” (“chocolate”) is the sweet food asked for; “来一块” needs a noun for something edible. “给我来一块巧克力” fits. The other words are verbs or adjectives.

items.text:
A：你哪儿不舒服？
B：我肚子疼，很（ ）。
items.explain: “难受” (“uncomfortable, feeling ill”) describes a sore stomach in reply to “哪儿不舒服”. It is an adjective after “很”. “活泼” (lively) does not describe illness.

example.text:
A：昨天的比赛你看了吗？
B：没看，太（ ）了。

items.text:
A：你认识那个人吗？
B：不认识，可是他刚才跟我（ ）了。
items.explain: “打招呼” (“to greet”) fits “不认识，可是他刚才跟我打招呼了”: a stranger said hello. The pattern is 跟 + person + 打招呼. “经历” is a noun and does not fit.

items.text:
A：这件事（ ）别告诉妈妈。
B：放心吧，我不会说的。
items.explain: “千万” (“by all means”) strengthens a request: “千万别告诉妈妈” (be sure not to tell Mom). It goes before a negative command. “放心吧” in the reply fits. “稍微” does not.

items.text:
A：你能（ ）等我一下吗？
B：好的，你快点儿。
items.explain: “稍微” (“slightly, a little”) softens the request: “稍微等我一下” = wait for me a moment. It is an adverb before the verb 等. “千万” would be too forceful here.

items.text:
A：他的汉语说得真好。
B：是啊，他（ ）很努力。
items.explain: “确实” (“indeed, really”) confirms the praise: his Chinese is good, and “他确实很努力” agrees. It is an adverb before 很努力. “可惜” (what a pity) would not match.

items.text:
A：你在国外生活了十年，有什么有意思的（ ）吗？
B：有很多，我慢慢给你讲。
items.explain: “经历” (“experience”) is a noun after “有意思的”: “有意思的经历” means interesting experiences from ten years abroad. “打招呼” and “可惜” cannot be preceded by 的 in this way.

example.text:
A：昨天的比赛谁（ ）了？
B：我们班。

items.text:
A：你真的要去国外工作吗？
B：跟你（ ）的，我怎么会去国外呢？
items.explain: “开玩笑” (“to joke”) fits the denial: “跟你开玩笑的，我怎么会去国外呢”. The pattern is 跟 + person + 开玩笑. The question was a joke, not a real plan. “后悔” does not fit.

items.text:
A：你住在市中心吗？
B：不是，我住在（ ），离这儿有点儿远。
items.explain: “郊区” (“suburb”) answers “不是市中心”: I live in the suburbs, a bit far away. It is the noun after “住在”. “结果” and “通过” cannot be places.

items.text:
A：你买了那件衣服吗？
B：没买，现在有点儿（ ）。
items.explain: “后悔” (“to regret”) fits not buying the dress: “现在有点儿后悔”. It is a verb after “有点儿”. “结果” and “通过” do not describe feeling about a missed purchase.

items.text:
A：考试（ ）出来了吗？
B：出来了，我考了八十五分。
items.explain: “结果” (“result”) is the noun in “考试结果出来了吗”, and the reply gives the score, 85. “出来” collocates with 结果. “通过” would be a verb, not the result.

items.text:
A：你是怎么找到这份工作的？
B：是（ ）朋友介绍的。
items.explain: “通过” (“through, by means of”) in “是通过朋友介绍的”: found the job via a friend. The pattern is 是 + 通过 + means + 的. “结果” and “郊区” do not express means.

example.text:
A：你们酒店（ ）早饭吗？
B：有，早上七点到十点，在一楼。

items.text:
A：你爸爸（ ）怎么样？
B：很好，他从来不生气。
items.explain: “脾气” (“temper, disposition”) is what “从来不生气” answers: his temper is good. “脾气怎么样” is a standard question. “流行” and “正常” do not fit a person’s nature.

items.text:
A：你怎么走回来了？
B：最后一班车已经走了，我（ ）走回来。
items.explain: “只好” (“have no choice but to”) fits no last bus, so I walked back. It is an adverb before the verb 走. “首先” and “提供” do not express the lack of options.

items.text:
A：这首歌现在很（ ）。
B：是啊，我经常听到。
items.explain: “流行” (“popular, in vogue”) fits a song that is often heard: “这首歌现在很流行”. It is an adjective after “很”. “正常” (normal) does not explain why you hear it often.

items.text:
A：医生，我的检查结果怎么样？
B：一切都很（ ），别担心。
items.explain: “正常” (“normal”) fits a doctor’s reassurance: “一切都很正常，别担心” (everything is normal, don’t worry). It is an adjective after “很”. “流行” does not apply to test results.

items.text:
A：学好汉语要怎么做？
B：（ ）要多听多说，其次要多读多写。
items.explain: “首先……，其次……” (“first…, second…”) lists steps: first listen and speak, second read and write. “其次” in the reply fixes the pair. “首先” is a conjunction opening the list.

example.text:
A：你的（ ）是什么？我给你寄过去。
B：我写给你吧。

items.text:
A：这个问题我们明天再（ ）吧。
B：好，今天大家都累了。
items.explain: “讨论” (“to discuss”) takes “这个问题” as object; the reply about everyone being tired confirms postponing the meeting. “再讨论” fits “明天再……吧”. “支持” does not take 问题.

items.text:
A：我想出国留学。
B：好啊，我们都（ ）你。
items.explain: “支持” (“to support”) fits “我想出国留学”: we all back you. It is a verb with 你 as object. “讨论” would be odd after the good news. “浪费” has the wrong meaning.

items.text:
A：从这儿到机场要多长时间？
B：（ ）一个小时。
items.explain: “大约” (“about, approximately”) gives an estimate of time: about an hour. It is an adverb before the number “一个小时”. “大约” answers “要多长时间” as a rough figure.

items.text:
A：这些菜还没吃完呢。
B：带回家吧，别（ ）。
items.explain: “浪费” (“to waste”) fits uneaten food: take it home so as not to waste it. “别浪费” is a negative command. “支持” and “讨论” do not suit this.

items.text:
A：你怎么又写错了？
B：我太（ ）了，下次一定注意。
items.explain: “马虎” (“careless, sloppy”) explains the repeated mistake, and “下次一定注意” confirms it. It is an adjective after “太”. “地址” is a noun, and “大约” is an estimate; neither describes a person.
